lots.title: Lift Servicing, Maintenance, Repair, Minor Refurbishment and Compliance Management
lots.description: London Borough of Bexley appoints a single Supplier to provide servicing, maintenance, repair, minor refurbishment and compliance management for lifts within the corporate estate, with the option to include schools and other sites on a call-off basis. Service includes a 365-day, 24/7 call-out response for entrapments, failures and safety incidents across 24 lift assets at 12 sites (subject to change). Contract commencement Sept 2026, initial term 3+2 years subject to performance. Integration with the Council's CAFM (Civica/TF Cloud) is mandatory.
requirements: Provide 24/7/365 call-out response for entrapments, failures and safety incidents (attendance: Entrapment/Life Safety within 1 hour target; Operational Failure within 4 hours; Nuisance/Minor Fault next working day).
All new or substantially modified equipment must comply with EN 81-20:2020 and EN 81-50:2020 (or UK-designated equivalents) and the Lifts Regulations 2016 (UK).
Where buildings fall within scope of BS 9991:2024, evacuation lift requirements must be considered during project design and lifecycle planning.
Track emerging standards (e.g., ISO 8100-1/-2 convergence) and apply successor or designated standards without delay.
Prepare an annual PPM schedule per site/asset, distinguishing statutory tasks (e.g., LOLER thorough examinations) from best-practice servicing; execute PPMs per manufacturer guidance and EN 13015.

Monthly servicing of passenger service lifts (ride quality, levelling, door operation/guards incl. non-contact light curtain per EN 81-20, alarm/emergency comms, pit/car-top/shaft/machine room inspection, lubrication, cleaning, defect logging).
Quarterly (or manufacturer-recommended) servicing for service lifts, platforms and access lifts; for person-carrying platform lifts LOLER thorough examination interval set to 6 months.

LOLER thorough examination by competent person at statutory intervals (typically 6-monthly for passenger/goods-passenger lifts; 12-monthly for goods-only). Reports must meet LOLER Sch. 1 and be retained. Complete certificates within 28 days of insurer report unless risk dictates sooner.
Apply SAFed LG1 for supplementary tests (UCMP, door systems, emergency release, refuge spaces, fire service/evacuation modes) when called by the competent person.
Use OEM or approved equivalent parts; safety-critical items must meet EN 81-20/50 performance where replaced; provide datasheets and declarations on request.

Operate a compatible work management platform with mobile workflows, photo evidence, asset updates and API/CSV exchange with Civica/TF Cloud; all work orders issued and updated via Civica/TF Cloud in real time.
Maintain a 24/7 telephony service for the Council, site contacts and the public (for entrapment calls) with call data available for audit.
Comply with HSW Act 1974, LOLER 1998, PUWER 1998, EAWR 1989, RIDDOR 2013, Workplace (H, S&W) Regulations; provide RAMS for all tasks and review annually or after incidents/changes.
Assume potential presence of ACMs unless confirmed; consult/sign site asbestos register; comply with Control of Asbestos Regulations 2012 and Council procedures.
Cooperate with Principal Designer/Principal Contractor under CDM 2015 for projects involving construction/refurbishment.

Engineers must be qualified and current, with ongoing training on EN 81-20/50, BS 7255:2023 (safe working on lifts), entrapment releases and site rules; maintain on-call rota 24/7 with English-proficient supervisors for customer-facing roles.
Submit Operating Manuals within 6 weeks of start: M&E Plan, PPM schedule by building, emergency and safety procedures, QA, hazardous materials, training plan, compliance logbooks.
Replace all references to the Data Protection Act 1998 with UK GDPR and Data Protection Act 2018; coordinate FOIA 2000 requests via the Council.
Deliver services consistent with the Equality Act 2010; provide inclusive support for vulnerable users and accessible notices.

Support carbon reduction plan: route optimisation, low-emission travel, LED car lighting, power-saving modes, regenerative drives where feasible, and recycling of components/packaging; provide environmental data for carbon reporting.
No sub-contracting without prior written consent; Supplier remains fully responsible for delivery and compliance, and passes down all safety/compliance/KPI/reporting obligations.
Maintain and annually test a Business Continuity Plan for major disruptions; ensure resilience for entrapment response and statutory inspections.
Deliver measurable social value outcomes aligned with Council priorities (local employment, apprenticeships, training, sustainability).
Mobilisation to establish governance, contacts, CAFM integration, key access, KPI baselines, asset validation and PPM regimes; all RAMS and emergency procedures before go-live.

Provide daily call-out summaries, weekly performance dashboards, monthly KPI reports, statutory compliance tracker, open quotes/defects register and insurer remedials progress; one monthly consolidated invoice via Civica/TF Cloud.

warnings.message: Lot number 7 is inferred from the document title '6278 - Draft specification - Lot 7' and from the header line 'Lift Specification'. The document body does not itself enumerate its lot number; no contradiction with notice-level lot metadata was detected for Lot 7.

The tender specification does not cite any CPV codes. cpv_codes is left empty; daemon-side enrichment or notice-level CPV should supply codes if needed (e.g., 50750000 'Lift-maintenance services' is the natural match but is not evidenced in this document).

The document defines KPI-based performance monitoring but does not publish a scored evaluation model (no price/quality weightings, no sub-criterion percentages). Emitted evaluation_criteria describe the KPI/monitoring regime rather than a tender scoring matrix. Confidence kept at 50%.

The Docling markdown in document_extractions does not carry page boundaries (page_count=0, table_count=0, section_count=0). Evidence anchors use line-range (lines-N-M) and section heading text instead of true page numbers.

Docling markdown renders nearly every heading as '1.' (list-number reset per block). The literal numbering in the text is unreliable; anchors therefore use the heading title and the line range rather than the numeric prefix.

The extraction is titled '6278 - Draft specification - Lot 7' indicating this is a draft. Downstream decisions should treat requirements as provisional until confirmed against the final published specification.
